permission_scope.data_access: GitHub states that Copilot cloud agent can research a repository. For the cloud agent, outbound network access is restricted by a firewall enabled by default; organization owners can configure allowed external hosts. Checked 2026-08-15.
permission_scope.unattended_actions: GitHub states that the cloud agent can plan and make code changes and create pull requests; sessions can also be started automatically on a schedule or event. The work is proposed on a branch/pull request, not silently merged. Checked 2026-08-15.
permission_scope.requires_approval: GitHub instructs users to review changes before merging. Where repository rules require approvals, the initiating user's approval of a Copilot pull request does not count and another reviewer must approve. Checked 2026-08-15.
permission_scope.quoted_source: "research a repository, plan and make code changes, and create pull requests for you to review" — https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent (checked 2026-08-15)

provenance.builder: GitHub, Inc. (a Microsoft subsidiary). Product documentation: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/cloud-agent (checked 2026-08-15).
provenance.governance_model: Repository and organization policy controls govern availability; Business/Enterprise administrators must enable the agent, repositories can be opted out, a default network firewall restricts outbound access, and changes are surfaced through pull-request review. Sources checked 2026-08-15: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/cloud-agent/access-management and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents.

incident_record.incident: CVE-2025-53773: NVD records command injection in GitHub Copilot and Microsoft Visual Studio that could allow an unauthorized attacker to execute code locally; Microsoft supplied CVSS 3.1 score 7.8 High. NVD's affected configuration identifies Visual Studio 2022 17.14 before 17.14.12. This affects a Copilot/Visual Studio agent-mode surface, but the NVD entry does not establish that GitHub's cloud-hosted coding agent itself was affected.

A public GitHub issue reports that Copilot CLI on Windows could hang indefinitely when running a full Vitest suite while the same command completed in a normal terminal. This is user-reported reliability evidence and was open when checked, not a vendor-confirmed incident.

A public GitHub issue reports that a single Copilot CLI session consumed 80–100 premium requests as tool/thinking turns progressed despite an estimate of one request. The issue was closed when checked; the page does not expose a vendor root-cause statement.

A public GitHub issue reports that after a June 16 service outage, all Copilot CLI models appeared blocked or disabled and new sessions could not start. The issue was closed when checked; this is user-reported reliability evidence.

complaint_evidence.summary: Discussion of the GitHub Copilot coding-agent launch questioned the absence of disclosed internal-usage figures and raised concerns about product evidence. This is opinion/complaint evidence, not proof of a technical failure.

Issue #2591 alleges unexpectedly high premium-request consumption during one session. It is directly observable user-reported complaint evidence but lacks a public vendor root-cause statement on the page.
Issue #3308 alleges an indefinite hang for full Vitest suites in the Copilot CLI terminal on Windows, with a file-output workaround.

addressed: ASI02 Tool Misuse — permission prompts and configurable allowed/denied tools are documented for CLI; pull-request review limits direct deployment of cloud-agent changes. Sources: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/cli-best-practices (checked 2026-08-15).

ASI03 Identity & Privilege Abuse — organization policies, repository opt-out controls, and required independent approval under protected-branch rules are documented. Sources: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/cloud-agent/access-management and https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-on-github/use-copilot-agents/review-copilot-output (checked 2026-08-15).

ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities — GitHub documents configurable MCP servers and a default outbound firewall/allowlisting boundary, which partially addresses external integrations. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents (checked 2026-08-15).

ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution — GitHub documents interactive permission prompts for local command execution and a pull-request review boundary for cloud-agent code changes. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents (checked 2026-08-15).
